A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAP-TTA study. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–Q support comparison; the shorter v2 mainly reflects layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOD-detection, narrative-generation, adaptation, ablation, and human-evaluation results, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a no-trigger, 16-segment configuration to Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix K retain the same triggered LoRA updates, SafeBank routing, and offline diagonal preconditioner. No-trigger adaptation already existed in v1; its additional evaluation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: WritingPrompts, RealToxicityPrompts, WikiText-2, HolisticBias, and the English human-evaluation population are retained. The longer generation configuration changes experimental settings within the existing narrative task.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds NoTrig to its ablation comparison, using 16 segments. No-trigger preconditioning already appeared in Table 3, but its participation in Table 4 is new. The external baselines and other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds evaluation with epsilon=0, 16 segments, and 128 tokens per segment. This supplements the existing protocols rather than replacing the default four-segment setting; retained sampling, scoring, and human-evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Table 4 row extends the ablations with a combined no-trigger and longer-generation configuration. Because both threshold and segment count differ, it does not isolate their effects. Existing sensitivity analyses, diagnostic plots, and generated examples are retained.

E5.justification: The OOD confidence intervals, Table 3 uncertainty notation, paired tests, five-rater protocol, and Appendix P agreement statistics are unchanged. The added ablation uses the existing point-estimate reporting practice without new seed or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Table 4 newly reports NoTrig/16-segment PPL 13.040, fluency 0.313, BB Bias 0.442, trigger rate 1.000, and update time 0.850 seconds. These are results under an added configuration. Section 5.1 also corrects eight-segment PPL from 13.180 to 14.774, matching Table 4 and Appendix L already in v1.

T1.justification: The KL projection, exponential tilt, trust-region derivation, descent and drift bounds, and Appendix K assumptions and preconditioner construction are unchanged. Mathematical passages receive only wording or layout edits.

C1.justification: The abstract strengthens 'mitigates catastrophic forgetting' to 'prevents catastrophic forgetting,' making the assertion categorical. The principal OOD-debiasing, latency, and fluency contributions otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: The detailed discussion retains the same safety–quality–latency trade-offs and cross-backbone interpretation. Limitations concerning detector dependence, SafeBank coverage, English-only evaluation, deployment overhead, and absent formal safety guarantees remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The artifact pointer changes from an anonymous repository to the named GitHub repository hshen13/debias_tta, and a front-page footnote states that code is available. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and runtime details are retained; repository availability itself cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds discussion of efficient LoRA variants and training-free activation steering, accompanied by seven new references, including QLoRA, DoRA, and activation-steering work. This broadens related-work context without redefining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, makes scattered grammatical and terminology edits, updates author and affiliation notes, and adds explicit appendix cross-references. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 gain metric-direction arrows, Table 4 gains a row and adjusted formatting, and several captions are revised. Short appendix sections are consolidated and material is repaginated; the existing plots and diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Section 5.1 to agree with Table 4, adding a limited ablation, and improving related-work context, table labels, and access instructions modestly improve accuracy and usability. These gains are tempered by the abstract's stronger claim of preventing catastrophic forgetting, which receives no new direct forgetting evaluation.
